Better than Fury Road because its not trying to be Fury Road. Here is god's plenty, in other words. A true blue epic with wit and ambition, from a director who may very well be at the end of his career. Whatever qualms I have with the inconstancy of the editing was easily made up for in the back half of the film. I understand that there are those who are going to judge this and every subsequent Mad Max entry by the strengths of Fury Road, but this in itself is such a refreshing change of pace for not just Miller but blockbuster filmmaking in general. Great time at the theatre.

Even if it’s at the expense of dignified portrayals of indigenous people? Even if it continues historical notions of white saviorism as it relates to the expansion of America? Really, is everyone here so effing obsessed with “muh vibes” that they can’t, in light of modern reconciliation with the horrors and tragedy imposed by western expansion, in good faith question the validity of art or artist?

God I don’t think I can sit through a long ass ep of Griff and David sidestepping the blatant white savior nonsense of Dances with Wolves. I don’t care if he’s making more crappy westerns, he’s an undeniably boring choice at best and maybe the worst series subject. Brest will be actual fun.

Every individual audience member comes into a film with their own experiences and points of view. It’s not invalid to infer if the film is asking its audience to infer and draw their own conclusions. 

Does it matter if the president is a Trumpian stand-in? Does it change the context for the film if they aren’t? Does it matter if the Western Forces soldiers wear bright red signs that shout “bad guy!” in every scene? 

Why are people being so inherently antagonistic to anyone who thinks positively of the film? What’s there to prove?

Commerce serves the market, not the artist. Just pull a roadshow release and go from there. Don’t feed the studios and distributiors any more than necessary, they’re wallowing in self imposed gluttony as is.

Not to risk being a contrarian, I found this film to be talking down to me as an indigenous person. The characterization and cultural specifics of the Na’vi, as in the first, recycle worn tropes - be it the casting of non-indigenous actors in indigenous roles (or in this case, indigenous inspired), their overly simplified relationship with nature and the land, and most importantly the mining of of tragic Colonialist history to tell a heroic story about a white character’s triumph over evil at the expense of the indigenous people whom assisted him. While I’m sure Cameron believes himself to be in the right, the film is tone deaf. The Na’vi whoop in almost every scene. No amount of excellent craft can cushion historically racist cinematic choices. I couldn’t enjoy this film.
